answer: Cross-epoch divergence scoring: each agent’s actions are embedded as a vertex in a rolling behavior graph, keyed by an onyx hash of its prior-epoch vector. The rule: an identity must stay within a bounded distance of its own trajectory; sudden reallocation from dormant inlet patterns to high-value flows flags it. Attacker cost: must sustain coherent behavior across many epochs for every synthetic identity, making mass creation computationally and operationally expensive.
